en: control of a company; right of management

examples.en: The president handed over management of the company to his son.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 경영권을 놓고 다투고 있어요.
examples.en: The two companies are fighting over control of management.

examples.ko: 대주주는 경영권 방어를 위해 주식을 더 샀어요.
examples.en: The major shareholder bought more shares to defend management control.

examples.ko: 아버지는 경영권 문제로 형제들과 사이가 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: My father fell out with his brothers over the issue of who controls the business.

examples.ko: 새 투자자가 회사 경영권을 인수하겠다고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The new investor said it would take over control of the company.

examples.ko: 경영권이 바뀐 뒤 회사 분위기가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: After control of the company changed hands, the atmosphere changed.

explain: '경영권을 쥐다/넘기다/지키다'처럼 써요. 회사를 운영하는 힘을 말하고, 재산의 주인이 되는 '소유권'과는 달라요. 뉴스에서 주식이나 가족 회사 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 큰아들은 경영권을 지키려고 주식을 더 샀어요.
phrases.en: The eldest son bought more shares to hold on to control of the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사를 운영하는 힘을 빼앗기지 않으려고 애쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone tries not to lose the power to run a company.
phrases.en_equiv: to keep control of a company

phrases.example: 형제가 경영권 다툼을 벌여서 뉴스에 나왔어요.
phrases.en: The brothers fought over control of the company and it made the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사를 누가 운영할지를 두고 싸우는 일을 하나의 말로 묶어 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase for a fight over who will run a company.
phrases.en_equiv: a fight for control of a company

phrases.en: The president lost control of the company because of debt.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지키다'와 반대로 회사를 운영하는 힘이 다른 사람에게 가 버렸을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of keeping it: the power to run the company has gone to someone else.
phrases.en_equiv: to lose control of a company

explain_en: It goes with verbs like '경영권을 쥐다', '넘기다' and '지키다'. It is the power to run a company, which is different from '소유권' (ownership). It appears often in news about stocks and family businesses.

examples.en: I got demerit points for not turning in homework.
If the demerits exceed ten points, they contact the parents.
I ran a signal and got 15 penalty points.
At this school, being late adds up demerits.

examples.ko: 벌점을 받으면 상점으로 줄일 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you get demerits, you can also reduce them with merit points.
My driver's license was suspended because of penalty points.

explain: 벌점은 학교나 운전면허, 스포츠에서 규칙을 어길 때 쌓이는 점수예요. 반대로 잘했을 때 받는 점수는 '상점'이라고 해요. '벌점을 받다', '벌점이 쌓이다', '벌점을 매기다'처럼 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I got demerit points for being late to class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙을 어겨서 점수가 생겼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you got points for breaking a rule.

phrases.en: If demerit points pile up, your license is suspended.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점수가 조금씩 늘어날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the points slowly grow in number.

phrases.en: I got merit points for doing my homework well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벌점'과 반대로 잘했을 때 받는 점수예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '벌점'; points for doing well.

explain_en: Penalty points given for breaking rules, as in schools or driving. 벌점 are points that pile up when you break rules in school, driving or sports. The opposite, points for good behavior, are '상점'. It goes with '벌점을 받다', '벌점이 쌓이다' and '벌점을 매기다'.

en: to restructure; to rearrange; to reshuffle

examples.ko: 일정을 재조정해야 하면 하루 전까지 알려 주세요.
examples.en: If the schedule needs to be adjusted, please tell us a day ahead.

examples.ko: 환율이 크게 올라서 수출 가격을 재조정하고 있어요.
examples.en: The exchange rate rose sharply, so we are readjusting export prices.
The meeting times overlapped, so I rearranged the appointment.

examples.ko: 예산을 재조정하면 새 프로젝트를 시작할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If we rearrange the budget, we can start the new project.
The school decided to revise its vacation plans.
The person in charge adjusted my working hours for me.

explain: 이미 정한 일정, 가격, 예산 같은 것을 상황에 맞게 다시 맞출 때 써요. 약속 시간만 바꾸는 가벼운 일에는 '바꾸다'나 '미루다'가 더 자연스러워요. 회사나 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: This year's budget was readjusted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 하는 것이 아니라 바뀐 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Passive form describing the result of readjustment.

phrases.en: Material costs rose, so prices need to be readjusted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '재조정'을 앞말과 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun collocation using 재조정.

phrases.en: I adjusted the timetable again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say it.

explain_en: Use it when you adjust something already decided, such as a schedule, price or budget, to fit the situation. For simply changing an appointment time, '바꾸다' or '미루다' sounds more natural. It shows up often at work and in the news.

examples.en: You need to tune the guitar strings for the sound to be right.

examples.ko: 두 회사는 회의 일정을 조율하고 있어요.
examples.en: The two companies are coordinating the meeting schedule.
The team leader smoothed out the differences of opinion among the staff.
Let's adjust our schedules and meet next week.
Could we adjust the price a little?

examples.ko: 서로 입장을 조율하는 일이 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy to reconcile each other's positions.

explain: 악기 소리를 맞추는 것에서 나와서, 사람들 사이의 일정이나 의견을 서로 맞추는 데도 써요. 직장에서 '일정을 조율하다'는 아주 자주 들려요. '조정하다'는 수치나 시간을 바꾸는 쪽이고, 조율하다는 여러 쪽이 서로 맞춰 가는 과정이 느껴져요.

phrases.en: We decided after adjusting our opinions with the team members.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 생각을 맞춰 갈 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing for bringing different views into agreement.

phrases.en: Our times don't match, so we need to coordinate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조율'을 명사로 써서 서로 맞춰야 하는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using 조율 as a noun to say that the sides need to be aligned.

phrases.en: Please coordinate the schedule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직장에서 일정을 맞춰 달라고 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request at work to sort out a schedule.

explain_en: The word comes from tuning instruments and is also used for matching schedules or opinions between people. '일정을 조율하다' is very common at work. '조정하다' is more about changing a number or time, while 조율하다 conveys several sides adjusting to each other.

en: to make someone participate; to involve

examples.en: The teacher gets every student involved in class.
We got the kids to take part in cleaning.
I want to involve the employees in the meeting.
If you involve guests in the event, they enjoy it more.
An event that involved the residents was held.
Don't force your younger sibling to join.

explain: 내가 참여하는 게 아니라 다른 사람이 참여하게 만들 때 써요. '참여하다'는 내가 하는 것, '참여시키다'는 상대를 끌어들이는 것이에요. 목적어에는 '을/를', 행사나 활동에는 '에'를 써요.

phrases.en: I want to get the children involved in the event too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 끌어들이고 싶은 바람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express a wish to get others involved.

phrases.en: We got the guests to join the game, so the mood got better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유나 방법을 이어 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used to give a reason or a method.

phrases.example: 선생님은 그 학생을 경기에 참여시키지 않았어요.
phrases.en: The teacher did not let that student take part in the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가를 일부러 빼는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes deliberately leaving someone out.

explain_en: Causative — get people engaged, e.g. in class activities. Use this when you make someone else take part, not when you take part yourself. '참여하다' is what you do on your own; 참여시키다 brings someone else in. The person takes 을/를, and the event or activity takes 에.

en: to supplement the personnel; to recruit

examples.en: The company filled its staff shortage.

examples.ko: 올해 안에 직원 다섯 명을 충원할 예정이에요.
examples.en: We plan to add five employees within this year.
The team can only run if it adds players.
It took time to fill the vacancy.

examples.ko: 아직 충원하지 못해서 모두 야근을 해요.
examples.en: We haven't been able to add staff yet, so everyone works overtime.

examples.ko: 새로 충원한 사람들이 잘 적응하고 있어요.
examples.en: The newly added people are adjusting well.

explain: '보충하다'는 물건이나 내용에도 쓰지만 '충원하다'는 사람, 즉 인원이나 인력을 채울 때만 써요. '인력을 충원하다', '결원을 충원하다'처럼 목적어가 정해져 있어요.

phrases.en: We posted a notice to fill the vacancies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빈자리를 채운다는 뜻의 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The typical phrase for filling empty positions.

phrases.en: It's a busy season, so we need to add staff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일손이 모자랄 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common expression when workers are short.

phrases.en: The empty position will be filled soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '충원하다'의 피동형으로, 자리가 채워질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used when a position gets filled.

explain_en: To add people to a group or organization short of members (부원) '보충하다' can be used for things or content too, but '충원하다' is only for filling people, meaning headcount or manpower. Its objects are fixed, as in '인력을 충원하다' and '결원을 충원하다'.

examples.ko: 경찰과 소방서의 공조 덕분에 구조가 아주 빨랐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to cooperation between the police and fire department, the rescue was very quick.

examples.ko: 이번 사건은 국제 공조 덕분에 해결됐어요.
examples.en: This case was solved thanks to international cooperation.
Cooperation between Korea and the US is always solid.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 공조를 바라는 목소리가 커요.
examples.en: Calls for the two countries to cooperate are growing louder.
We set up a joint system and responded to the problem.

examples.ko: 여러 기관의 공조 없이는 해결하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to solve without cooperation among several agencies.

explain: 나라나 기관이 서로 힘을 합칠 때 쓰는 뉴스 단어예요. 친구끼리 같이 하는 일에는 '협력'이나 '같이 하다'가 더 자연스러워요. '국제 공조'처럼 굳은 말로 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 큰 범죄를 막으려면 국제 공조가 필요해요.
phrases.en: International cooperation is needed to stop big crimes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 나라가 함께할 때 쓰는 굳은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fixed phrase for several countries working together.

phrases.example: 두 나라는 새로운 공조 체제를 만들었어요.
phrases.en: The two countries created a new cooperation system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 일하는 틀이나 방식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the framework or way of working together.

phrases.example: 정부가 이웃 나라와 공조를 강화하기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The government decided to strengthen cooperation with its neighbor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 협력을 더 단단하게 한다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making cooperation stronger and is often seen in news.

explain_en: Formal coordination among states or agencies — police, diplomacy (국제 공조) A news-style word for countries or agencies joining forces. For friends doing something together, 협력 or 같이 하다 sounds more natural. It often appears in fixed phrases like '국제 공조' (international cooperation).

t90.ax: Cooperation between Korea and the US is always solid.

en: party to a treaty; country concerned

examples.en: The countries involved in the dispute sat down at the negotiating table.
They say dialogue between the countries concerned is needed.
This problem has to be solved by the countries involved themselves.

examples.ko: 당사국의 동의 없이는 결정할 수 없어요.
examples.en: A decision can't be made without the consent of the country concerned.
The two countries are parties to that agreement.

examples.ko: 당사국이 아닌 나라는 의견만 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Countries that are not parties can only offer opinions.

explain: 조약이나 분쟁에 직접 관련된 나라를 말할 때 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 직접 관련 없는 나라는 '제3국'이라고 해요. 나라가 아니라 사람이나 회사일 때는 '당사자'를 써요.

phrases.en: The government of the country concerned stated its official position.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분쟁이나 조약에 직접 관련된 나라의 정부를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the government of a country directly involved in a dispute or treaty.

phrases.en: Please talk it over among the people involved first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라가 아니라 사람이나 회사가 직접 관련될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the directly involved party is a person or company, not a country.

phrases.en: A third country stepped in to mediate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 관련 없는 나라를 말하는 짝말이라서 '당사국'과 함께 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an uninvolved country, often contrasted with 당사국.

explain_en: State directly concerned in a treaty or conflict; diplomatic. It appears often in the news for a country directly involved in a treaty or dispute. A country not directly involved is a '제3국'. For people or companies, use '당사자' instead.

examples.en: When he was sued, he responded with a countersuit of his own.

examples.ko: 회사가 직원을 고소하자 직원도 맞고소를 했어요.
examples.en: When the company filed a complaint against the employee, the employee filed one back.
As the counter-complaints continued, the case became more complicated.
After consulting a lawyer, I decided to file a counter-complaint.
They even filed complaints against each other, but eventually settled.
They say you should decide on a counter-complaint carefully.

explain: '맞고소를 하다/맞고소에 나서다'처럼 쓰고 '맞고소하다'처럼 동사로도 써요. 주로 뉴스나 분쟁 이야기에서 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '나도 고소할 거예요'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: He didn't stay quiet and filed a counter lawsuit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맞고소'를 동사로 바꾼 형태로, 고소당한 사람이 거꾸로 고소할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, used when the sued person sues back.

phrases.en: The victim also stepped forward with a counter lawsuit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞서서 고소하려고 움직이기 시작했다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means starting to act to sue back, often used in news.
phrases.en_equiv: to take up a counter suit

phrases.en: I'm going to sue that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼저 고소하는 기본 동사이고, 이쪽도 고소하면 '맞고소'가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic verb for suing first; suing back becomes '맞고소'.

explain_en: It is used as '맞고소를 하다' or '맞고소에 나서다', and also as the verb '맞고소하다'. It mostly appears in news and dispute stories; in daily talk people may say '나도 고소할 거예요' instead.

examples.en: We do the cleaning on a rotating basis.

examples.ko: 주차 자리는 순번제라서 오늘은 제 차례가 아니에요.
examples.en: The parking spots are on a rotation, so it's not my turn today.
Our team decided to rotate who works late.
Thanks to the rotation system, complaints dropped a lot.
After we introduced a rotation system, the arguments stopped.
I suggested to my roommate that we take turns doing the dishes.

explain: 일을 차례대로 돌아가며 맡는 방식이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '돌아가면서 하다'라고 많이 하고, '순번제로 하다', '순번제를 도입하다' 형태로 써요.

phrases.en: We do the dishes in turns.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차례를 정해서 돌아가며 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means setting an order and taking turns.

phrases.en: The company introduced a rotating system for vacations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 그런 방식을 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when starting such a system anew.

phrases.en: We take turns cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '순번제'보다 이 말을 더 많이 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used more than '순번제' in daily conversation.

explain_en: It is a system where everyone takes a task in turn. In daily talk people often say '돌아가면서 하다', and '순번제' appears as '순번제로 하다' or '순번제를 도입하다'.

en: to unite; to associate; to ally

examples.en: The small shops join forces.
The two countries formed an alliance.
The students joined together and held an event.

examples.ko: 우리 동아리는 다른 동아리와 연합할 거예요.
examples.en: Our club will team up with another club.
Groups that join forces are growing in number.

examples.ko: 힘을 모으려고 연합했지만 결과는 좋지 않았어요.
examples.en: We joined forces to combine strength, but the result wasn't good.

explain: '연합하다'는 둘 이상의 단체나 나라가 하나의 목적으로 손을 잡을 때 써요. '같이 하다'보다 딱딱하고 '~와 연합하다'로 써요. 개인 두 사람이 힘을 합칠 때는 '힘을 합치다'를 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 우리 가게는 이웃 가게와 연합해서 행사를 열어요.
phrases.en: Our shop holds events by joining with neighboring shops.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~와' 뒤에 함께하는 상대를 넣어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the partner after '~와'.

phrases.en: The two companies joined hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연합하다'보다 쉽고 부드러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and softer than '연합하다'.

phrases.en: Let's join forces and try it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개인이나 작은 모임에도 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Natural for individuals or small groups too.

explain_en: Groups or organizations forming an alliance or league (작은 가게들이 연합하다) 연합하다 is used when two or more groups or countries join hands for one purpose. It is more formal than 같이 하다 and appears as '~와 연합하다'. For two individuals combining efforts, people more often say 힘을 합치다.

dis.h: groups form an alliance or league
gh: join parts or elements into one
casual: band together, or clump up
bind together tightly by a common bond
stand in solidarity for a cause

p.n: 결합 means merging or combining, not forming an alliance.

en: to be self-sufficient; to provide for oneself

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 채소를 직접 키워서 자급해요.
examples.en: My family grows vegetables ourselves and provides for ourselves.

examples.ko: 이 섬은 전기를 태양광으로 자급하고 있어요.
examples.en: This island supplies its own electricity with solar power.

examples.ko: 식량을 자급하지 못하는 나라는 수입에 의존해요.
examples.en: Countries that cannot feed themselves depend on imports.
My grandmother grows most of her own rice and vegetables.
You need a lot of investment to be self-sufficient in energy.

examples.ko: 시골에서는 옛날에 먹을 것을 자급하며 살았어요.
examples.en: In the countryside, people used to live by producing their own food.

explain: '식량을 자급하다', '에너지를 자급하다'처럼 필요한 것을 스스로 마련한다는 느낌으로 써요. 뉴스에서는 '식량 자급률'이 자주 나오고, '자급자족'이라는 말도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: That village lives self-sufficiently.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 것을 스스로 만들어 쓰는 생활을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for a life of producing what you need yourself.

phrases.en: Our country has a fairly high rice self-sufficiency rate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 양 중에 스스로 만드는 비율이라 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The share of needs produced domestically, common in the news.

phrases.en: I got the tuition together by myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '자급하다' 대신 쉽게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday alternative to '자급하다'.

explain_en: Supplying needed things yourself, such as food or energy, more formal. It is used as in '식량을 자급하다' or '에너지를 자급하다', with the feel of arranging what you need by yourself. In the news '식량 자급률' (food self-sufficiency rate) comes up often, and '자급자족' is also very common.

t90.ax: Countries that cannot feed themselves depend on imports.

en: to be concluded by agreement; to be reached (of a deal)

examples.ko: 오랜 협상 끝에 임금 문제가 드디어 타결됐어요.
examples.en: After long negotiations, the wage issue was finally settled.
The negotiations were settled, so the strike ended.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 무역 협상이 사흘 만에 타결됐어요.
examples.en: The trade talks between the two countries were settled in three days.

examples.ko: 이번에는 협상이 쉽게 타결되지 않을 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems the negotiations won't be settled easily this time.

examples.ko: 협상이 타결되었다는 소식에 직원들이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: Employees applauded at the news that the negotiations had been settled.

examples.ko: 양쪽이 조금씩 양보하면 문제가 빨리 타결될 거예요.
examples.en: If both sides give a little, the matter will be settled quickly.

explain: 협상, 교섭, 회담처럼 서로 입장이 달랐던 일이 합의로 끝날 때 써요. 주어는 사람이 아니라 '협상·문제' 같은 일이고, 사람이 주어면 '타결하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 밤샘 회담 끝에 협상이 극적으로 타결됐어요.
phrases.en: After an all-night meeting, the negotiation was settled dramatically.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마지막 순간에 갑자기 합의가 이루어졌을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when an agreement comes together suddenly at the last moment.

phrases.en: The meeting ran long, but the negotiation was not settled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합의에 이르지 못한 상태를 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for when no agreement has been reached.

phrases.example: 두 나라가 오랜 대화 끝에 합의에 이르렀어요.
phrases.en: The two countries reached an agreement after a long talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 뜻이 맞아 결론을 낸다는 뜻으로 '타결되다'와 비슷하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means coming to a shared conclusion, used much like 타결되다.

explain_en: It is used when something where the sides disagreed, such as negotiations or talks, ends in agreement. The subject is the matter itself, like '협상' or '문제', not a person; with a person as subject you use '타결하다'.

examples.en: Residents were shocked by the news of the school mergers and closures.
The district office is reviewing merging and cutting departments.

examples.ko: 인구가 줄면서 작은 학교의 통폐합이 이어져요.
examples.en: As the population shrinks, small schools keep being merged or closed.
The restructuring changed the staff's work a lot.
Opinions are divided on merging and closing public agencies.

examples.ko: 통폐합은 비용을 줄이려고 하지만 불편도 생겨요.
examples.en: Mergers and closures aim to cut costs, but they cause inconvenience too.

explain: '통합'은 하나로 합치는 것, '폐지'는 없애는 것인데, '통폐합'은 이 둘을 묶은 말로 학교·기관·부서를 줄이거나 합칠 때 써요. 주로 뉴스나 행정 글에서 나와요.

phrases.example: 시는 작은 학교 세 곳을 통폐합했어요.
phrases.en: The city merged and closed three small schools.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통폐합'에 '하다'를 붙인 동사로, 줄이거나 합치는 주체를 주어로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form. The body doing the merging or closing is the subject.

phrases.example: 인구가 줄어서 우리 동네 학교가 통폐합됐어요.
phrases.en: Because the population dropped, our neighborhood school was merged and closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합쳐지거나 없어진 쪽을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the merged or closed organization is the subject.

phrases.en: The office of education announced a merger and closure plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이나 학교를 정리하려는 계획을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for a plan to consolidate institutions or schools.

explain_en: Merging and closing down organizations such as schools or offices. '통합' means joining into one and '폐지' means abolishing; '통폐합' bundles both and is used when schools, agencies, or departments are merged or cut. It appears mainly in news and administrative writing.

en: to permit; to allow; to tolerate

examples.ko: 이 건물에서는 음식을 먹는 것을 허용하지 않아요.
examples.en: Eating food is not allowed in this building.
The school allows the use of cell phones.
My parents allowed me to come home late.
The company decided to allow working from home.
Let's do it within what the rules allow.
I'm looking for a home that permits pets.

explain: '허용하다'는 규칙이나 기관이 '해도 된다'고 정할 때 써서 글과 안내문에 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '허락하다'나 '되다'를 써요. 반대말은 '금지하다'예요.

phrases.en: My parents allowed my trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 사람이 '해도 돼'라고 할 때 써요. '허용하다'는 규칙이나 기관에 더 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in everyday talk when a person says 'you may'. '허용하다' fits rules and institutions better.

phrases.en: Taking photos is allowed here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 허용하는지보다 '해도 되는 상태'를 말할 때 써요. 안내문에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on the state of being allowed rather than who allows it. Common on signs and notices.

phrases.example: 시험 중에는 휴대폰을 허용할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: We can't allow phones during the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안 된다고 단호하게 말할 때 써요. 규칙이나 기관의 입장을 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say firmly that something is not allowed. It sounds like a rule or an institution speaking.

explain_en: Allow something within rules, general policy. 허용하다 is used when a rule or institution says something is allowed, and it is common in written notices. In everyday talk, 허락하다 or the plain 되다 is more usual. The opposite is 금지하다.

dis.h: let something be allowed; tolerate it

p.n: 허가 makes it sound like official approval is needed; 허용 is a general policy.

t90.ax: My parents allowed me to come home late.
